events.dek: eThekwini’s inaugural council meeting adjourned on 24 November without electing a mayor, deputy mayor or speaker, and IOL, DailyNews and the Sunday Tribune report the council is reconvening as parties finalise coalition positions. IOL reports ANC-MK coalition talks have stalled over key positions, and EWN reports former mayor Cyril Xaba is among five councillors who have resigned.
brief: Several outlets report the council adjourned without filling a leadership position to allow coalition talks to conclude; IOL, DailyNews and the Sunday Tribune report it reconvenes to elect a mayor and speaker, with IOL saying all eyes are on eThekwini.

IOL earlier reported the ANC and MK sealed an eThekwini deal with the ANC seeking two of the top four positions, but now reports the talks have stalled over key positions; the MK Party says its mayoral candidate has an “unblemished record”, IOL and The Mercury report.
eNCA reports the DA has proposed to 'donate' the eThekwini mayorship to the ANC, and DailyNews reports ActionSA rejected DA pressure over the eThekwini coalition.

EWN reports former mayor Cyril Xaba is among five eThekwini councillors who have resigned; the Mail & Guardian reports allegations of dirty deals and sudden resignations, and The South African reports the IFP and EFF mayoral hopefuls will not take up their seats.
eNCA reports the first sitting went ahead despite a KwaZulu-Natal Cogta directive to delay it, which IOL, DailyNews and the Sunday Tribune report the city manager challenged.

events.h: The DA secures a five-party coalition in Emfuleni after a sitting collapses
events.dek: ANC, EFF and MK councillors disrupted Emfuleni’s mayoral election sitting, and Nova News reports it collapsed. News24 reports the DA has secured a five-party coalition to take control of the municipality, and the DA now accuses the Gauteng government of wilful delays.
brief: News24 reports chaos as ANC, EFF and MK councillors disrupted the Emfuleni mayoral election sitting, Nova News reports the sitting collapsed, and The South African Star reports police were called in despite a DA warning.
The DA’s Ashor Sarupen condemned what he called EFF violence at the Emfuleni council sitting, in a statement carried by Politicsweb.
News24 reports the DA secured a five-party coalition to take control of Emfuleni, giving up MMC posts, the speaker and the chief whip.
The DA says, in a statement carried by Politicsweb, that the Gauteng government’s wilful delays in Emfuleni will not delay democracy, and eNCA reports Emfuleni faces a crucial leadership vote.

events.h: The DA takes Knysna and Bitou but is shut out of Theewaterskloof, Laingsburg and Langeberg
events.dek: News24 reports the ANC joined other parties to take control of Theewaterskloof, IOL and the Cape Times report ActionSA formed a Laingsburg coalition with the PA and ANC, and the Cape Argus reports an ANC-PA coalition won Langeberg, all leaving the DA out. The Cape Argus reports the DA has taken Knysna and Bitou, and SABC News reports Matzikama council will sit on Thursday after a deadlock over an EFF councillor.
brief: News24 reports the ANC and other parties took control of Theewaterskloof, shutting out the DA; the Cape Argus, Cape Times and IOL report the DA warning this could derail financial recovery.

IOL and the Cape Times report ActionSA formed a coalition with the PA and ANC in Laingsburg, leaving the DA out, and SABC News reports Matzikama council sits on Thursday after a deadlock over an EFF councillor.
IOL reported a three-party coalition agreement put the DA in line to govern Knysna; the Cape Argus reports the DA has taken Knysna and Bitou, while an ANC-PA coalition won Langeberg.

News24 reports the DA and FF Plus entered coalitions in some hung councils; IOL reported the DA began talks with 16 councils hung, and named deputy mayor and speaker candidates for seven Western Cape municipalities.
IOL and the Weekend Argus carry an argument that the opposition’s voice in Cape Town is growing smaller and meeker.

events.h: The ANC leaves coalition choices to its provinces and regions
events.dek: EWN and Dan Corder report the ANC’s NEC has let provinces and regions decide coalitions, affecting over 100 hung councils, and SABC News and IOL report the NEC resolved that DA coalitions should be a last resort. IOL and The Common Sense report the ANC moved Fikile Mbalula’s coalition briefing to Friday, and eNCA reports the ANC is to brief on the outcomes of the talks.
brief: EWN asks whether the ANC has given provinces and regions the final say; Dan Corder says the NEC let regional bodies choose, affecting well over 100 hung councils, and SABC News and IOL report the NEC resolved that the DA should be a 'last resort'.

IOL and Smile 90.4FM report the ANC postponed its coalition announcement again, IOL and The Common Sense report it pushed Mbalula’s coalition briefing to Friday, and eNCA reports the ANC is to brief on the outcomes of tough coalition talks.

Newsnote reports the ANC asserting there is consensus as talks near conclusion; Business Day reports the ANC is seeking a foothold in hung councils, and EWN quotes an analyst warning of a 'death spiral'.

IOL reports the SACP drawing a line over coalition support and left-wing parties rejecting an ANC coalition with the DA; The Common Sense reports the SACP called a Sol Plaatje deal with the DA a “betrayal” and argues ANC indecision has left a power vacuum.

TimesLIVE and Business Day report Ramaphosa says he is 'not resigning' after the election setback, IOL reports tensions over Ramaphosa and working with the DA, and SABC News reports Malatji saying the ANC’s decline goes beyond its current leadership.

events.h: MK’s Nomathamsanqa Mthembu becomes uMhlathuze mayor as the ANC, DA and IFP take KwaDukuza
events.dek: IOL, News24, SABC News and Central News South Africa report the MK Party and ANC have taken uMhlathuze, with Nomathamsanqa Mthembu elected mayor and News24 saying the pact sidelined the IFP and DA. In KwaDukuza, The Citizen reports a last-minute deal has put the ANC, DA and IFP in control, while The Witness reports GPU parties have closed ranks in some councils as MK and ANC talks continue.
brief: IOL, News24 and SABC News report the MK Party’s Nomathamsanqa Mthembu was elected uMhlathuze mayor; News24 says the ANC-MK pact sidelined the IFP and DA, and Central News South Africa calls the MK-ANC takeover a political power shift.

Central News South Africa reports the ANC and MK Party formed a coalition to take control of uPhongolo Municipality, and The Witness reports MK Party and ANC talks are continuing while GPU parties close ranks in some councils.
The Citizen reports a last-minute coalition deal saw the ANC, DA and IFP take control of KwaDukuza, and The Witness reports the ANC and DA partnered to keep the MK Party out of government there.
The Citizen reports a coalition deal in Endumeni delivered a surprise mayoral victory for the IFP.

The National reports coalition deals are reshaping municipal power in KwaZulu-Natal and exposing divisions in the ANC, and IOL reports DA leadership will attend the uMngeni inauguration, one of only 10 outright wins in the province.
